generations.prompt: Production animation cels for a 2D cel-shaded arcade beat-em-up. Reference 1 defines EXACT character identity, anatomy, palette, clothing, silhouette and carried objects. IRON SHOGUN: bulky armored warrior in black and gold, horned helmet, red belt, crouched walk, same-length sword held at constant low angle in front. Keep the full weight and texture of the armor. Sword at belt height, directed forward, fully inside frame. Preserve the helmet horn design and the two identifiable boots. Make exactly EIGHT isolated, entire, RIGHT-facing figures regularly laid out in a four column by two row grid, generous clear gutters including outermost edges. True transparent background; no floor/shadow/FX/text/labels. Ref 2 is skeletal choreography only; ref 3 is an approved male character animation for rhythm and leg ordering ONLY, do not adopt his wardrobe or face. Same scale, camera, lighting and model across all frames. Outlines clean like the identity reference. Same serious expression as idle. Draw near anatomical RIGHT leg and arm in light, far LEFT leg slightly darker and behind it when they overlap. Upper body in three-quarter right-facing profile, face to screen right. Cloth and hair lag smoothly. Never repeat the same leg leading in both rows. For the very FIRST CEL of row TWO, the entire lighter near thigh from the visible hip to the knee extends BACK towards SCREEN LEFT and connects to the rear shoe; the darker far leg leads forward to screen RIGHT. The near forearm is in FRONT of the rib cage. This contrasts with the first cel of row ONE, where the near knee and shoe lead and the near forearm trails behind the rib cage. Do not duplicate the top row. Each row must depict different near-leg silhouette and occlusions at the hip. Two half cycles with precisely equal and opposite stride and knee lift. Crouched, bent-knee, low center of gravity samurai armored WALK cycle. Top row: near/right leg stepping forward onto heel with far leg stretched back on toe; next near leg flat under weight, dark far shoe lifting behind; then near leg straight under pelvis, far knee bent passing it; finally far leg swinging forward and near leg behind. Bottom row opposite: FAR/left thigh and shoe forward on heel in the first pose, right/near leg stretching backward with near/right foot visibly behind, near arm forward. Follow with loading, passing, opposite foot swing. A continuous cycle where eighth frame leads back to first. In contact poses toe-to-toe span about 31% of standing height. Pelvis stays fixed, support foot moves uniformly backwards.
